extracted.intended_audience: CIHR review committee members (chairs, scientific officers, reviewers), program staff, and applicants to CIHR priority-driven initiatives
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for conducting peer review and adjudication of applications to CIHR priority-driven funding initiatives, including reviewer roles, evaluation criteria, scoring, adjudication models, and procedural safeguards. Intended to govern how applications are assessed, scored, ranked, and communicated for funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of review
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR’s principles of review are: confidentiality; absence of conflict of interest; fairness; and, transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles underpin the integrity of the review process and guide reviewer behaviour and process design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Information provided by applicants is protected by the Privacy Act and is made available to external assessors for reviewing purposes only. Committee members must not divulge contents or use information for purposes other than peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members must not approach or communicate with applicants about reviews; applicants must not contact committee members about application status. Written review materials are made available to applicants after funding decisions; reviewer identities are not revealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A conflict of interest exists where a participant's duties and responsibilities with regard to the review process conflict with private, professional, business or public interests (real, perceived or potential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include personal/professional relationships, financial interest, close affiliation, supervision/trainee relationships, frequent interactions in the last six years, recent collaborations or shared funding. All committee members must declare conflicts and abide by the Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality Policy of the Federal Research Funding Organizations (COIC). CIHR staff resolve uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must exercise rigorous judgement, be impartial and reasonable, and take into account the particular context of each application in a balanced way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive, quality reviews should point out strengths and weaknesses for improvement. CIHR may remove comments deemed sarcastic, flippant, arrogant, inappropriate, or factually incorrect regarding CIHR policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in review
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are evaluated using the application requirements and review criteria in the funding opportunity; Scientific Officer (SO) notes capture deliberations and reviews and SO notes and reviewer reports are shared with applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR may publish committee membership lists and funding decision databases. SO notes and reviews provide transparency into determining factors and budget/term decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers must have (individually or collectively) the required experience and/or expertise, as determined by CIHR, to assess the quality and/or potential impact of the proposed research within the funding opportunity context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review panels include academic and non-academic reviewers (industry, government, community) to ensure appropriate perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of review processes (committee meeting vs. virtual review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review for priority-driven initiatives is typically conducted using committee meetings (in person or teleconference) or virtual review (electronic, at-home reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee meetings involve discussion and consensus scoring with reviewers asked to score within ±0.5 of consensus; virtual review relies on written scores and reports from assigned reviewers and may allow discussion only if score discrepancies warrant it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance review (adjudication model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Used to assess alignment of an application with a specific research theme in the funding opportunity; typically conducted prior to peer review. Applications deemed relevant proceed to the next step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied when alignment to targeted research components is critical to the FO objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific review (adjudication model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard review mechanism assessing scientific excellence using a clear set of evaluation criteria measuring key aspects of proposals relative to the funding opportunity's scope and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers rate each criterion individually and provide a single overall score. Weighting may be applied but criteria are typically treated equally. Only applications exceeding the fundable threshold based on consolidated overall score are considered for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review (adjudication model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses separate scores/ratings for Potential Impact and Scientific Merit, typically for projects that engage knowledge-users throughout the research process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential Impact reflects importance to knowledge-users and likelihood of substantive, sustainable impact. Only applications that exceed the fundable threshold on both Potential Impact and Scientific Merit are considered; the mean of the two scores is used for final rating and ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — Research approach
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five typical CIHR criteria: Research approach (assesses the methods and feasibility of the proposed research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider factors relevant to the funding opportunity and focus comments on factors most relevant to the rating; emphasis may be placed on specific criteria to meet program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — Originality of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five typical CIHR criteria: Originality (assesses novelty and innovation of the proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality should be judged in the context of the FO objectives and relative to the research field; may be weighted differently by specific funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — Applicant(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five typical CIHR criteria: Applicant(s) (assesses the qualifications, productivity, and suitability of the investigator team).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess productivity and progress broadly in alignment with DORA (see DORA guidance entry). Consider context (leave history, career stage, area(s) of research, experiential knowledge, diverse career paths, family responsibilities, pandemic impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — Environment of the research
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five typical CIHR criteria: Environment (assesses institutional support, infrastructure, and suitability of the environment to carry out the research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how the institutional setting will contribute to project success; regional and institutional factors may be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — Impact of the research
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five typical CIHR criteria: Impact (assesses the potential of the research to improve health outcomes, services, policy, practice, or other meaningful impacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact may be judged differently depending on the adjudication model (e.g., separate Potential Impact score under Merit Review). Consider expected substantive and sustainable effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: DORA-aligned assessment of productivity and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR follows the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA): scholarly outputs include a broad range of contributions and impacts and are not limited to published journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess productivity and progress broadly (publications, reports, books, guidelines, datasets, code, tools, training, mentorship, community engagement, standards, software, commercialized products) and impacts (policy/practice influence, health outcomes, societal outcomes, distinctions-based and culturally safe research). Do not use publication/citation counts or journal-based metrics in isolation; Journal Impact Factors should not be used as surrogate measures of individual paper quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating scale and funding threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR commonly uses a 0.0–4.9 rating scale (4.9 highest). Applications must receive a score of 3.50 or higher to be considered for funding. Ratings are assigned qualitative descriptors to guide reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard descriptors and ranges: Outstanding 4.5–4.9 (May be Funded – Will be Discussed), Excellent 4.0–4.4, Very good 3.5–3.9, Fair 3.0–3.4 (Not Fundable – May or May Not be Discussed), Poor 0.0–2.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review rating interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: For Merit Review, separate scores are used for Potential Impact and Scientific Merit with qualitative descriptors (e.g., Potential Impact: Extremely Significant/Very Significant/Significant/Moderate/Limited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applications exceeding the threshold rating of 3.50 on both Potential Impact and Scientific Merit will be considered for funding; the mean of the two scores determines final rating for eligible applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binning process
rubrics_metrics.description: The binning process groups applications to distinguish those that should or should not be discussed, focusing discussions on meritorious applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in conjunction with rating scale to prioritize committee time; can be used to identify competitive vs. non-competitive applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members may opt not to discuss an application if the average initial scores are clearly above or below the fundable score (high or low streamlining).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If streamlined, initial scores are averaged to make the final score; SO notes will not be taken and therefore not provided to the applicant. An application may be streamlined if: binning shows non-competitive, clearly above or below funding cut-off projection, average initial ratings < 3.50, and/or no objection from other committee members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of committee members and composition considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are selected for knowledge, expertise and/or experience. Membership as a whole should cover the range of research areas and methodologies, reviewing capability in both English and French, regional representation, and gender representation proportionate to the Canadian health research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR program staff make final decisions on membership, consulting relevant groups and following COIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Chair responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Chair responsibilities include suggesting members, working with CIHR staff on agendas and streamlining, managing conflicts of interest, moderating meetings, ensuring participation, ensuring adherence to DORA, summarizing discussions, ensuring consensus rating is reached, and ensuring budget/term and ethical considerations are discussed and recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair does not rate or vote. Chair may appoint delegates when conflicted and may propose re-discussion of inconsistently reviewed applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Officer (SO) responsibilities and SO notes content
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Officers support the Chair, take official notes of committee discussions (SO notes), ensure notes align with DORA, read back notes for validation, summarize budget/term changes and ethical flags, finalize and post SO notes within 5 working days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO notes should provide clear, concise, objective and constructive feedback; identify determining factors in the evaluation, describe how budget/term were determined, include strengths/weaknesses in alignment with DORA, address issues not captured in reviewer reports, and describe how reviewer disagreements were reconciled. SOs do not rate or vote. CIHR will not edit SO notes without SO approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer duties and written review expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers must provide a critical assessment and constructive feedback based on the funding opportunity objectives and evaluation criteria, consider all factors and strengths/weaknesses in relation to each criterion and DORA, emphasize factors most relevant to the rating, comment on budget and provide formal budget/term recommendations with reasons, flag issues as required, and provide an initial rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are assigned to a minimum of two reviewers. Written reports and initial ratings should be submitted on ResearchNet (usually one week before and no later than the day before the meeting). Once submitted as final, reviewers can view others' reviews but cannot modify them prior to the meeting; after the meeting reviewers have one week to upload changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader role and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers are assigned to read an application, serve as formal discussants at the committee meeting, and aid in reaching consensus; they are not required to submit a written review but may be asked to provide an initial (unrecorded) score for discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should prepare speaking notes and be ready to discuss the application. Their initial score, if provided, is not recorded and is for discussion only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus rating and voting procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: At committee meetings reviewers announce initial ratings, discuss the application, and the Chair seeks a consensus rating. If consensus cannot be reached, the Chair declares the consensus score (usually the mean of revised scores rounded as needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All committee members (except Chair and SO) then cast confidential individual votes within ±0.5 of the consensus rating. The final rating is the average of these confidential votes. Internal reviewers are not bound to the consensus rating.
